headline: 'He Just Gave Up On Us': Jets' Arniel Talks Hellebuyck Trade, Devils' Decision To Sit Goalie Out
take:
The Hockey News reports that Jets coach Scott Arniel, asked about New Jersey's decision to sit Connor Hellebuyck ahead of his return to Canada Life Centre, did not hold back, saying "He just gave up on us." As Daily Faceoff posted, citing Chris Johnston, Hellebuyck says he'll reveal why he requested a trade out of Winnipeg when he speaks to reporters in the city on Tuesday morning.

The numbers say Hellebuyck has been fine in New Jersey, not a savior. So far this season, in five games, he has a .913 save percentage and has saved 1.46 goals more than an average goalie would have against the same shots, a small but positive start. Last season he saved 3.43 goals above expected across 57 games. The Devils are 13-5-0 and controlling play, with a 59% share of expected goals (the quality of chances each side creates), though their goaltending overall sits 5.2 goals below expected, so the crease isn't what's driving them. Winnipeg is 7-8-3 with a 48% share and has scored 7.2 fewer goals than its chances suggest. That gap is the bigger story for the Jets than any one goalie.
